summary: EA and DICE's large-scale combined-arms shooter series, spanning PC originals, console spin-offs, live-service entries, free-to-play experiments, and modern cross-platform releases.

primary.why: Battlefield 1942 began as a PC-first multiplayer shooter, and Windows is the only practical high-fidelity route with the Road to Rome and Secret Weapons expansions.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Windows release with the latest community/server-browser setup available; document whether using original discs, digital preservation files, and expansion packs.

primary.why: Battlefield Vietnam was released for Windows, making the PC version the only complete route.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Windows release with current compatibility fixes and document any community server setup.

primary.why: Battlefield 2 is a PC-first entry, and Windows with its expansion/booster content is the most complete route.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Windows Complete Collection or equivalent install with current community master-server/server-browser setup; document expansions and patch version.

entries.title: Battlefield 2: Modern Combat

emulation.notes: Prefer Xbox hardware/backward compatibility; Xenia only if compatibility is verified.

primary.why: Modern Combat is the console-specific Battlefield 2 spin-off; the Xbox 360 version is the highest-fidelity release.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Xbox 360 version on Xbox hardware/backward compatibility where available; use sixth-generation versions only for comparison.

entries.remaster_caveats: Online-era features depend on service availability.

entries.title: Battlefield 2142

primary.why: Battlefield 2142 is a PC-first entry; Windows with Northern Strike content and community server restoration is the complete route.
primary.how_to_play: Play on Windows with the current community master-server/server-browser restoration and Northern Strike content documented.

entries.remaster_caveats: Official online infrastructure is legacy; document community service used.

entries.title: Battlefield: Bad Company

emulation.notes: Prefer Xbox hardware/backward compatibility; emulation only after compatibility verification.

primary.why: Bad Company never came to PC; Xbox 360 via modern Xbox compatibility is the cleanest high-fidelity route for the campaign after online services were retired.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Xbox 360 version through Xbox backward compatibility if available; treat multiplayer as historical because EA retired online services.

entries.remaster_caveats: No PC port or remaster; multiplayer preservation is limited by server shutdown.

primary.why: Battlefield Heroes was a Windows free-to-play online game, but EA shut the service down in July 2015, so the archive route is historical documentation rather than normal play.
primary.how_to_play: No official current play route; preserve client media, footage, and documentation only unless a legally documented preservation server is available.

emulation.notes: Emulation does not restore official service; use only for preservation research.

primary.why: Battlefield 1943 was a console-only downloadable entry; online services were retired, so Xbox 360/backward compatibility is the best preservation target for installed copies.
primary.how_to_play: No normal official multiplayer route remains; preserve installed Xbox 360 copies/media and document server shutdown state.

entries.title: Battlefield: Bad Company 2

primary.version: PC release with Vietnam expansion and preservation/community-server path
primary.why: Windows is the highest-fidelity route for the campaign, multiplayer-era content, and Vietnam expansion; official services were retired, but the PC build remains the best preservation target.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Windows campaign and Vietnam content; document whether using any community server restoration such as Project Rome and note that official EA online services were retired.

entries.remaster_caveats: Document official shutdown and community-server route separately.

primary.why: Battlefield Online was a Windows online-only Korean-market remake of Battlefield 2, and its servers were shut down in 2013.
primary.how_to_play: No official current play route; preserve client footage, documentation, and server-shutdown context only.

primary.why: Battlefield Play4Free was a Windows online-only free-to-play game and EA shut it down in July 2015.
primary.how_to_play: No official current play route; preserve client media, footage, and documentation only unless a legally documented preservation route exists.

entries.title: Battlefield 3

primary.why: Windows is the highest-fidelity route and Premium Edition contains the full DLC map/content suite.
primary.how_to_play: Play Battlefield 3 Premium Edition on Windows; document EA App/Steam state, PunkBuster/server-browser setup, and DLC installation.

entries.remaster_caveats: Document live server and anti-cheat compatibility.

entries.title: Battlefield 4

primary.why: Windows Premium Edition is the highest-fidelity route and includes the full major DLC suite.
primary.how_to_play: Play Battlefield 4 Premium Edition on Windows; document EA App/Steam state, DLC installation, server browser, and anti-cheat setup.

entries.remaster_caveats: Document server, DLC, and anti-cheat state.

entries.title: Battlefield Hardline

primary.why: Windows is the highest-fidelity route and remains the best preservation target as console online support is being retired.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Windows version with all DLC/Ultimate content installed; document EA App/Steam state and server availability.

entries.remaster_caveats: Document server status because console services are ending/ended while PC remains the practical route.

entries.title: Battlefield 1
entries.definitive_edition: Battlefield 1 Revolution/current complete edition on Windows

primary.why: Windows is the highest-fidelity route, and Revolution/current complete editions include the Premium Pass map/content suite.
primary.how_to_play: Play Battlefield 1 Revolution/current complete edition on Windows; document DLC installation, server browser, and anti-cheat state.

entries.remaster_caveats: Live server population varies; document capture date.

entries.title: Battlefield V
entries.definitive_edition: Battlefield V Definitive/current edition on Windows

primary.why: Windows is the highest-fidelity route and the definitive/current release includes the post-launch content state.
primary.how_to_play: Play Battlefield V Definitive/current edition on Windows; document server browser, anti-cheat, and patch state.

entries.remaster_caveats: Live server population varies; document capture date.

entries.title: Battlefield 2042

primary.why: Battlefield 2042 supports the largest-scale feature set on PC/current-gen platforms; Windows is the highest-fidelity and most configurable route.
primary.how_to_play: Play the current Windows release; document season/content state, server availability, anti-cheat, and whether the account has required specialists/weapons unlocked.

entries.remaster_caveats: Online-only game; capture date and patch version matter.

entries.title: Battlefield 6

primary.why: Battlefield 6 launched on Windows, PlayStation 5, and Xbox Series X/S; Windows is the highest-fidelity and most configurable route for campaign/multiplayer capture.
primary.how_to_play: Play the current Windows release through EA App, Steam, or Epic; document season, patch, anti-cheat/Secure Boot requirements, and whether using Standard or Phantom Edition content.

entries.remaster_caveats: Active live-service title; revisit as seasons and roadmap content change.

entries.title: Battlefield REDSEC

primary.why: REDSEC is a free-to-play Battlefield 6 companion focused on Battle Royale, Gauntlet, and Portal; Windows is the most configurable route.
primary.how_to_play: Play the current Windows REDSEC client through EA App, Steam, or Epic; document season, patch, anti-cheat requirements, and account progression.

entries.remaster_caveats: Free-to-play live service; revisit as modes and seasons change.
